comparison: Perfect agreement on triple mutant analysis (C8, C31-C33, C38, C78). Both evaluations find the data well-supported and praise the sophisticated triple mutant approach showing additive defects and complete disorganization. OpenEval and peer reviewers both rate this as SUPPORTED with no concerns raised.

Perfect agreement on concluding significance statements (C101-C102). Both evaluations affirm the study's importance and clinical relevance. OpenEval and peer reviewers both rate these claims as SUPPORTED, with reviewers explicitly calling it 'important' and 'significant' work.

Strong agreement on discussion and conceptual interpretations (C89-C92, C94-C99, C100). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN noting speculative elements, while peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the discussion appropriately integrates findings with literature and acknowledges limitations. Both recognize mechanistic details remain to be determined.

Strong agreement on distinct misprojection trajectories (C29-C30, C34-C37, C79-C84). Both evaluations find the comparative analysis of different phenotypes well-supported by quantitative measurements. OpenEval and peer reviewers both rate as SUPPORTED, with no concerns about the interpretation of distinct guidance mechanisms.

Agreement on mechanistic speculation (C73-C76). Both evaluations recognize these as speculative hypotheses. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN noting they require future testing, while peer reviewers also rate as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging these are proposals not specifically evaluated and that mechanism remains to be determined.

Strong agreement on main conclusions and model (C9, C11, C60-C61, C85-C88). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED noting the model integrates data well though sequential steps are speculative. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, affirming the demonstration of multi-factorial mechanisms while accepting that specific mechanistic details remain speculative.

Strong agreement on receptor mutant analysis (C10, C50-C59, C71). Both evaluations find the phenotypic similarity between ligand and receptor mutants well-supported by quantitative data. OpenEval and peer reviewers both rate as SUPPORTED with no concerns raised about the receptor analysis.

Strong agreement on reinterpretation of Ntn1 function (C62, C64-C67, C70, C77). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED noting the distinction from prior studies, though acknowledging reliance on literature comparison. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, accepting this revised understanding as part of the study's contribution.

Partial overlap on genetic labeling data (C6, C23-C28). OpenEval R3 focuses on Neurog1-CreERT2 labeling demonstrating DRG origin. Peer R1 covers broader misprojection findings including both C5-C6 and C18-C28. Both rate as SUPPORTED with explicit reviewer affirmation and no concerns about the genetic labeling approach.

Strong agreement on bifurcation preservation (C7, C39-C42, C68). Both evaluations find the DiI single axon data showing >90% bifurcation across genotypes well-supported. OpenEval and peer reviewers both rate as SUPPORTED, with reviewers explicitly noting bifurcation is unaffected by the mutations.

Strong agreement on quantitative angle measurements (C43-C49). OpenEval R4 emphasizes statistical analysis showing additive defects. Peer R4 accepts the quantitative tracing supporting distinct and additive functions. Both rate as SUPPORTED with careful quantification highlighted as a strength.

Strong agreement on wholemount staining showing misprojections (C5, C16-C22). OpenEval R2 focuses on quantitative line scan measurements at multiple locations. Peer R1 covers these claims along with genetic labeling data. Both rate as SUPPORTED with explicit reviewer affirmation of the core observations.

Agreement on Ntn1 expression data (C16). OpenEval R2 includes this as part of broader misprojection analysis. Peer R8 specifically notes this expression data is presented without critique. Both implicitly support this as background context for functional studies.

Agreement on DCC expression data (C51-C52). OpenEval R7 includes this as supporting context for receptor mutant phenotypes. Peer R9 notes this is cited from previous work and presented without critique. Both treat this as accepted background information rather than primary findings.

OpenEval R1 evaluates foundational anatomical and functional knowledge (C1-C2, C12-C15) as SUPPORTED by literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers did not separately evaluate these background/contextual claims that establish the biological framework for the study.
